newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-UK traders buy calls in BP, BSkyB, BritGas.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-UK traders buy calls in BP, BSkyB, BritGas.

text.p: Expectations of good times ahead brought bullish trading to the UK stock options market on Friday, dealers said.
One of the main deals was in British Petroleum where 1,000 January 750 calls were bought at 101-1/2p and in a separate trade, 1,000 January 800 calls bought at 4-1/2p.
These deals continue a spate of call option buying executed by the same broker throughout the week.
At the close of business on the London stock exchange, BP shares were 8p higher at 694-1/2p. The company will announce third-quarter figures on November 5.
A surge in the shares of satellite television operator British Sky Broadcasting Group encouraged one trader to buy 400 December 700 calls at 8-1/2p.
BSkyB shares climbed 24-1/2p to 649-1/2p and the company will hold its annual general meeting on November 1.
Over in British Gas there was a buyer of 250 March 200 calls at 5-1/2p. The underlying shares closed up 2p at 187-1/2p.
Elswhere, in National Westminster Bank, the main trade was from a buyer of straddles. The deal was to buy 260 January 700 puts and calls at 23p and 32p each.
For a profit by January expiry, NatWest shares need to either go below 645p or go above 755p. The shares ended the day with a gain of 1-1/2p to 700-1/2p.
And in British Airways a bull spread was established by buying 250 January 600 calls at 21p and selling 250 January 650 calls at 8p.
The underlying shares were up 8-1/2p to 584p and the strategy will make a maximum profit of 37p at expiry if the shares go above 650p.
